description: 50 MW hyperscale campus behind a weak 40 MW grid connection: critical IT with UPS battery, gas genset fleet, rooftop PV, genset/battery expansion candidates. Tagged and ready for an Energy Hub study.

ledger.label: Connection ramp limit
ledger.note: assumed: 10% of the 40 MW connection per minute; RfG/DCC set no ramp limit for a demand facility, so this is a placeholder of the order a network operator writes into a connection offer for large loads

ledger.label: Power oscillation limit
ledger.note: assumed: peak-to-peak power oscillation at most 1 % of the connection in the 0.1-2 Hz band (forced-oscillation concern for large loads, NERC 2025 large-loads white paper); no code value

ledger.label: Import efficiency
ledger.note: assumed: the grid_import Link's efficiency (losses = 1 - efficiency); what reaches the site side of the PoC Link. Losses further in (transformers, UPS) are not in it

ledger.label: Fault level at the PoC
ledger.note: assumed: short-circuit power at the PoC (grid); the SCR and rapid-voltage-change screenings read it

ledger.label: Reliability goal (LOLE)
ledger.note: assumed: the recommended pack's target_lole_h (3 h/yr); the reliability study certifies the site against it

ledger.label: Grid supply forced-outage rate
ledger.note: assumed: generic public data, not this site's: SAIDI 3.945 min/yr / (60 x 8760); CEER-ECRB 7th Benchmarking Report on the Quality of Electricity and Gas Supply (2022), Table 2-18: TSO SAIDI and SAIFI excluding exceptional events, 2011-2018, median year. The PoC Link's own outage data is separate and not in these figures

ledger.label: Grid supply mean time to repair
ledger.note: assumed: generic public data, not this site's: SAIDI 3.945 min/yr / (60 x SAIFI 0.135 per yr); CEER-ECRB 7th Benchmarking Report on the Quality of Electricity and Gas Supply (2022), Table 2-18: TSO SAIDI and SAIFI excluding exceptional events, 2011-2018, median year. The PoC Link's own outage data is separate and not in these figures
every asset in service on 2030-01-01; the week weighs a year and stands for each operating year, so nothing is annualised
